title: Wide Shot (WS)
description: A wide shot shows the subject in full environment, with bodies small enough that place still speaks. It is environment-forward coverage: do not isolate yet.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Size is a sentence. A wide shot maps who can reach the door, where the street goes, what weather is doing.
People are in the picture so we know the scale of the place, but the place is still talking. If you isolate too early, the scene loses its map.

It is the wrong tool when the beat is a face, a holster, or a head-to-toe costume portrait. It is also the wrong tool if the human has become an unreadable speck (extreme long shot) or if you only needed to declare the building before the scene (establishing as a job).
Use wide to keep geography in play, then change size when a new fact requires a tighter sentence.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Keep enough architecture, street, or weather that doors, paths, and weather remain readable. Bodies should not fill the height the way they do in a full-body portrait.

A 24mm in a room or a longer lens across a square can both be wide; the crop is whether place still speaks. Prompt: Wide shot of [Subject] in full environment, bodies small enough that place still speaks.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when you must not isolate yet: who can reach the door, how far the platform runs, whether two groups can see each other. Do not crop into a full-body fashion frame and call it wide, and do not use it as a blank postcard with no relation to the scene's paths.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Full Body makes the complete figure the subject, head to toe, place as a border. A Long Shot is the person-in-world size: full figure plus geography, still a locatable human.
An Extreme Long Shot is speck-scale land. An Establishing Shot is a where-and-when job that often uses a wide.
A Master Shot is the action skeleton, which may be wide if blocking needs it. Wide is the environment-forward coverage attitude, not a synonym for those four.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Once Upon a Time in the West lets station and desert speak while bodies remain small enough that place is the sentence. Lawrence of Arabia can sit in this band when geography is still coverage, not yet a speck-scale subject.
Grammar: keep the map; do not portrait.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Say full environment and small bodies. Example: Wide shot of [Subject] in full environment, bodies small enough that place still speaks.
Name the door, the street, the weather. Do not write head to toe hero, mid-thigh cowboy, or speck.
For video, hold the geography; a tiny figure motion is enough.
Wide shot of [Subject] in full environment, bodies small enough that place still speaks.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a Full Body (person fills the height) or a Long Shot labeled wide with no coverage job. The tell is a costume portrait, or a speck landscape with no scene paths.
Fix: place still speaks, bodies small enough to keep the map, geography that the next cut can use.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Wide Shot in film?

A wide shot shows the subject in a full environment, with bodies small enough that place still speaks. It is environment-forward coverage, not a synonym for full body, long shot, or establishing shot.
Wide Shot vs Full Body

Full body is a complete figure as the subject, head to toe, with environment as a readable border. A wide shot keeps place in charge: doors, streets, and weather remain the sentence, and people are small enough not to isolate yet. If the person fills the frame height, you are in full body, not wide.
When should I use Wide Shot?
Use it when geography must stay in play and you should not isolate yet. Do not use it as a head-to-toe portrait, and do not use it when scale should go to a speck.
How do I prompt Wide Shot for AI image or video?
Write Wide shot of [Subject] in full environment, bodies small enough that place still speaks. Name architecture and weather. Keep people from filling the height of the frame.
